claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy contains both FCC and BCC phases.
Eutectic phase boundaries in the as-cast alloy have inherently weaker interfacial bonding.
A post-solidification heat treatment can selectively strengthen the eutectic interfaces.
The heat treatment can strengthen the interfaces without significantly changing phase fractions or the overall microstructure.
During elevated-temperature wear-corrosion, mechanical strain concentrates at weak eutectic interfaces.
Strain concentration at weak eutectic interfaces causes microcrack formation.
Interface-associated microcracks disrupt protective oxide films.
Microcracking impairs regeneration of the protective oxide films.
Loss or impaired regeneration of protective oxide films accelerates localized corrosion.
Localized corrosion further weakens the eutectic interfaces.
Corrosion-induced interface weakening intensifies mechanical wear.
The reciprocal interaction among interface weakening, microcracking, oxide disruption, corrosion, and wear creates synergistic coupled degradation.
The interface-strengthened heat-treated alloy will have lower total degradation than the as-cast baseline.
The heat-treated alloy will have a lower wear rate because it forms fewer microcrack-induced defects.
The heat-treated alloy will exhibit less localized corrosion because strengthened interfaces improve oxide-film retention.
The proposed coupling is expected to operate at approximately 400°C in chloride-rich conditions under controlled mechanical loading.
The coupling effect may differ outside the stated temperature, chloride, and loading regime or when other degradation mechanisms predominate.
